'''Alan G. Marshall''' (May 26, 1944 – June 6, 2025) was an American analytical chemist who devoted his scientific career to developing a scientific technique known as [[Fourier transform ion cyclotron resonance]] (FT-ICR) [[mass spectrometry]], which he co-invented.

He was born in Bluffton, Ohio, in 1944, and earned his bachelor's in chemistry from [[Northwestern University]] (1965) and Ph.D. in chemistry from [[Stanford University]] (1970).  His first academic appointment was at the [[University of British Columbia]].  In 1980, he moved to the [[Ohio State University]] where he remained until 1993.

He was the Robert O. Lawton Professor of Chemistry and Biochemistry at [[Florida State University]] and director of the Ion Cyclotron Resonance Program at the [[National High Magnetic Field Laboratory]].

He was a fellow of the [[American Chemical Society]], [[American Physical Society]], and the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]], and received numerous awards, including the 2000 Thomson Medal given by the [[International Mass Spectrometry Foundation]]; the 2007 [[Chemical Pioneer Award]], given by the [[American Institute of Chemists]];<ref>{{cite web |title=Chemical Pioneer Award Winners |url=https://www.theaic.org/award_winners/chem_pioneer.html |website=[[American Institute of Chemists]] |access-date=13 June 2025}}</ref> the 2012 [[William H. Nichols Medal]], given by the New York Section of the [[American Chemical Society]];<ref>{{cite web |title=NY-ACS Nichols Medalists |url=https://www.newyorkacs.org/nicholsmedalists.html |website=newyorkacs.org |access-date=13 June 2025}}</ref> and the 2012 Pittsburgh Analytical Chemistry Award, given by the Society for Analytical Chemists of Pittsburgh.

Marshall died on June 6, 2025.<ref>{{cite web |title=Alan George Marshall Obituary |url=https://www.tallahassee.com/obituaries/psar1204956 |website=tallahassee.com |access-date=23 November 2025 |language=en |date=15 June 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Schultz |first1=Edan |title=Remembering the MagLab’s Alan Marshall, pioneer in analytical chemistry |url=https://news.fsu.edu/news/university-news/2025/06/20/remembering-the-maglabs-alan-marshall-pioneer-in-analytical-chemistry/ |website=Florida State University News |access-date=23 November 2025 |date=20 June 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Strachan |first1=James |title=Honoring FT-ICR Pioneer Alan G. Marshall (1944–2025) |url=https://theanalyticalscientist.com/issues/2025/articles/july/honoring-ft-icr-pioneer-alan-g-marshall-1944-2025/ |access-date=23 November 2025 |work=The Analytical Scientist |date=3 July 2025 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Alan Marshall Obituary |url=https://neptunesociety.com/obituaries/tallahassee-fl/alan-marshall-12412252 |website=Neptune Society |access-date=5 September 2026 |language=en |date=6 June 2025}}</ref>
